source_title: Martinez's 'inexplicable' 83 seconds cost Man Utd and Carrick
source_excerpt:
Chelsea beat 10-man Man Utd to pile more pressure on Carrick
Lisandro Martinez made his way to the tunnel slowly and silently.
The whistles and jeers of the Chelsea fans were ringing in his ears. Manchester United coach Jonny Evans had a brief word, but Martinez didn't pay any attention.
As a player, Martinez has scaled the heights. He was part of the Argentina squad that won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the final last summer.
But at Stamford Bridge, when Michael Carrick needed his side to step up and his senior players to set an example, Martinez did the very opposite.
Eighteen days after Martinez called out United's summer recruitment, he suffered the kind of meltdown that would have left most United fans questioning whether that poor business involved not turfing the 28-year-old out of Old Trafford.
The former Ajax defender had been part of a much-improved United performance at Chelsea, and Carrick's team should have been ahead at half-time.
Even when Morgan Rogers gave the hosts a second-half lead, they had done enough for the visiting fans to believe a comeback was possible.
Instead, in the space of one minute and 23 seconds, Martinez committed two fouls that left Carrick's side 2-0 down and playing with 10 men - with Chelsea subsequently cruising to victory.
However this woeful period unfolds, it is unlikely Martinez's recklessness will be forgotten.
Has Martinez become a liability for Man Utd?
It was noticeable that Carrick did not look at Martinez as he made his way off the pitch.
He was more focused on trying to come up with a plan with his assistant Steve Holland to get through the rest of the game.
Asked afterwards if he felt let down by Martinez, Carrick said he had not had a chance to view the incident again.
"I've not seen it back, so I don't know if it was or not," Carrick said, adding: "It's a big moment in the game."
Carrick continued: "The second goal and losing a man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure."
For context, Martinez - already on a booking - chose the moment Estevao swung over the corner to try to block off Wesley Fofana at the far post.
In the process, he raised his elbow and caught the defender in the face. The incident was missed in real time but video assistant referee (VAR) James Bell advised referee Peter Bankes to go to the screen and the obvious conclusion was reached.
World Cup final official Darren Cann called Martinez's actions "inexplicable".
"He jumped into him, making no attempt to play the ball and not even looking at the ball as it came in from the corner," Cann told BBC Sport.
"Martinez was rightly sent off for two bookable offences, as well as conceding a needless penalty for the reckless challenge on Fofana."

'You can't have a liability in your team'
Chelsea v Manchester United - Michael Carrick post-match
United avoided the ignominy of a third successive three-goal defeat for the first time since 1961 thanks to a very tight VAR decision that ruled out Estevao's effort for offside.
Martinez will now be suspended for next Sunday's Premier League match with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.
"At 1-0 down, United are still in a decent position," former England and Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Sport. "You're still in the game.
"At 2-0 and down to 10 men, effectively the game is over.
"If the player sent off holds his hands up and says 'sorry, boys, I've let you down' it can defuse the situation, but the issue is that Martinez is making mistake after mistake at the moment."
Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole was rather more blunt on TNT Sports.
"In a Man United shirt, he's just at the scene of the crime too often," Cole said. "Whatever the next Man United phase is, I think Martinez's time at the club has run its course."
Former England midfielder Danny Murphy was equally scathing on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"Lisandro Martinez has got a lot to answer to, because the first goal was mainly his fault. The sending-off is absolutely ridiculous," said Murphy.
"Obviously, he is going to apologise in the dressing room, but his mindset is not right to play. You can't rely on him. He is a liability."
Asked whether he would play Martinez again, Murphy said: "No, I wouldn't, only because he looks like he has already gone. His head isn't right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.
"Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can't have a liability in your team. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.
"He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer."
The frustration shows for Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick at Stamford Bridge
If Martinez's actions were inexcusable, the reality is United were losing when they were reduced to 10 men.
For that, there has to be a large dollop of sympathy for Carrick.
In the first half, United were far better than they had been in three-goal margin losses to Como and Bournemouth. They were determined, concentrated, and focused. Sadly for Carrick, they weren't clinical.
Four excellent opportunities came and went. Bruno Fernandes and Amad both blazed off target when they should have done much better.
Chelsea keeper Mike Penders made two excellent saves. Even in the latter stages, Bryan Mbeumo's blistering shot couldn't find its way in.
On the bench, Carrick must have wondered if his luck will ever change.
Instead, United are nine games without a win in all competitions. It is their worst run since 1988-89.
They are teetering on the brink of dropping into the relegation zone for the first time since Sir Alex Ferguson's early days and on Tuesday welcome Serie A outfit Roma to Old Trafford knowing they need a win to keep their Champions League qualification hopes realistic.
Pre-match, the expectation had been Carrick would be in charge for that.
"There's no words I'm going to explain to you now that makes any difference," Carrick said. "It's not going to change it. We've got to move forward and win football matches, it's as simple as that.
"The way they went about it and played, the quality of football and the way we played in the first half definitely gives encouragement, and we've got to take that."

## मैच का मुख्य आकर्षण और लिसांद्रो मार्टिनेज का निष्कासन

स्टैमफोर्ड ब्रिज में खेले गए मुकाबले में चेल्सी ने मैनचेस्टर यूनाइटेड को हराकर कोच माइकल कैरिक की मुश्किलों को और बढ़ा दिया है। इस मैच के दौरान यूनाइटेड के डिफेंड्र लिसांद्रो मार्टिनेज का खेल चर्चा का विषय बन गया, खासकर उनके 83 सेकंड के भीतर किए गए दो बड़े फाउल, जिसके कारण उन्हें लाल कार्ड दिखाया गया।

मैच के दौरान मॉर्गन रोजर्स ने मेजबान टीम को बढ़त दिलाई थी, लेकिन यूनाइटेड की वापसी की उम्मीदें तब टूट गईं जब मार्टिनेज ने पेनल्टी क्षेत्र में वेस्ले फोफाना के खिलाफ कोहनी का इस्तेमाल किया। वीएआर (VAR) की मदद से रेफरी ने फासले का जायजा लिया और मार्टिनेज को दूसरा पीला कार्ड दिखाकर मैदान से बाहर भेज दिया। इसके बाद चेल्सी ने मुकाबले में अपनी पकड़ मजबूत कर ली और जीत दर्ज की।

## कोच माइकल कैरिक की प्रतिक्रिया और टीम की स्थिति

मैच के बाद कोच माइकल कैरिक ने स्वीकार किया कि दूसरा गोल खाना और एक खिलाड़ी का कम होना मैच का बड़ा मोड़ था। हालांकि, उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि उन्होंने घटना को दोबारा नहीं देखा है।

इस हार के बाद मैनचेस्टर यूनाइटेड सभी प्रतियोगिताओं में लगातार नौ मैचों से जीत से दूर है, जो 1988-89 के बाद से उनका सबसे खराब दौर माना जा रहा है। टीम अब प्रीमियर लीग तालिका में निचले हिस्से के करीब पहुंच रही है।

## खेल विश्लेषकों की राय

पूर्व खिलाड़ियों और विशेषज्ञों ने मार्टिनेज के प्रदर्शन की कड़ी आलोचना की है:

* **डैरेन कैन:** पूर्व वर्ल्ड कप फाइनल अधिकारी ने मार्टिनेज के खेल को 'अस्पष्ट' बताया और कहा कि उन्होंने गेंद को देखने का कोई प्रयास नहीं किया।
* **डैनी मर्फी:** उन्होंने माना कि मार्टिनेज का व्यवहार अस्वीकार्य है और इस समय टीम को उन पर भरोसा नहीं करना चाहिए।
* **स्टीफन वार्नॉक:** उनके अनुसार, 10 खिलाड़ियों के साथ खेलने के बाद मैच में वापसी करना लगभग असंभव हो गया था।

## आगामी चुनौतियां

लाल कार्ड मिलने के कारण मार्टिनेज अगले रविवार को एस्टन विला के खिलाफ होने वाले प्रीमियर लीग मुकाबले से बाहर रहेंगे। वहीं, मैनचेस्टर यूनाइटेड को मंगलवार को चैंपियंस लीग की उम्मीदों को जिंदा रखने के लिए रोमा के खिलाफ मैच खेलना है। क्लब के आधिकारिक चैनलों और खेल समाचार माध्यमों पर इस मुकाबले से जुड़ी विस्तृत जानकारी और विश्लेषण देखे जा सकते हैं।

en_body:
Manchester United faced further pressure following a defeat at Stamford Bridge, where defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off during a costly 83-second sequence that left Michael Carrick's side with 10 men.

## The Incident at Stamford Bridge

With Chelsea leading 1-0 following a second-half goal by Morgan Rogers, the match turned decisively during a brief spell. Martinez, who was already on a yellow card, attempted to block Wesley Fofana at the far post during a corner. Video assistant referee James Bell advised referee Peter Bankes to review the incident on the pitchside monitor, leading to a second yellow card and a penalty concession for a reckless challenge.

Former World Cup final official Darren Cann described the action to BBC Sport as inexplicable, noting that the defender made no attempt to play the ball. As a result of the red card, Martinez faces a suspension for the upcoming Premier League fixture against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

## Match Context and Team Struggles

Reporting indicates that United had shown an improved performance in the first half compared to recent losses against Como and Bournemouth, creating multiple opportunities through Bruno Fernandes and Amad that were either missed or saved by Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders. 

However, the defeat extends United's winless run across all competitions to nine matches, marking their worst sequence since the 1989 season. The team is also preparing to host Roma at Old Trafford in a fixture that carries significance for their Champions League qualification hopes.

## Analyst Reactions and Verification

Pundits offered strong criticism following the match:
* **Stephen Warnock** noted to BBC Sport that falling 2-0 behind with 10 men effectively ended the competitive contest.
* **Joe Cole** suggested on TNT Sports that the defender's time at the club may have run its course.
* **Danny Murphy** told BBC Radio 5 Live that the mindset of the player was currently unsuitable for selection.

When asked after the match if he felt let down, Carrick stated he had not yet reviewed the incident on video, while emphasizing that the second goal and the red card heavily influenced the outcome. Supporters and observers can verify the official match statistics, disciplinary records, and upcoming fixture details through the Premier League's official channels or accredited sports broadcasting networks.
